mainTopic: יהושע's childlessness and the greatness of תלמוד תורה; not disturbing a married couple's privacy; אביי's solution for a gentile who refuses to rent his rights in an alley
overview: This amud opens at the end of a proof from the previous amud: the verse 'נון בנו יהושע בנו' shows that יהושע had no son. רבי אבא בר פפא gives a different reason for this punishment: יהושע kept ישראל from פריה ורביה for one night. His source is the angel who met יהושע near יריחו and said 'עתה באתי'. The angel had come because ישראל were neglecting תלמוד תורה, and יהושע immediately spent the night deep in הלכה. A tradition that marital relations are forbidden while the ארון and שכינה are out of place explains the link to פריה ורביה. From the same story, רב teaches that תלמוד תורה is greater than the תמידין. רב then says it is wrong to sleep in a married couple's room. רב יוסף extends this even to when the wife is a נדה, and the גמרא rejects רבא's view that the guest deserves a blessing. Finally, the גמרא returns to עירובין: a gentile refuses to rent his rights in an alley, so אביי tells the residents to renounce their rights to one person. אביי defends this by saying רבנן do not decree for rare cases, and רבא's reaction begins on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse proving יהושע had no children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof from דברי הימים, whose family list of אפרים ends with יהושע and names no son after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'Nun his son, Joshua his son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the final verse of a proof that began on the previous amud. The verse shows that יהושע died without children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was that יהושע was punished for ruling in front of משה ('אדוני משה כלאם'). The punishment is going childless. This verse proves the punishment happened: the family list stops at יהושע, so he had no son to continue it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written: introduces a second verse
'Nun his son, Joshua his son' (דברי הימים א ז:כז)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the closing piece of a proof that started on the previous amud, about ruling הלכה in front of one's teacher. The proof works from silence: no child is listed after יהושע.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Nun his son, Joshua his son.'
phrases.notes: The list ends here, so יהושע had no son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in the previous section, on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That יהושע was punished by dying childless
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א ז:כז, where the genealogy ends with יהושע

steps.title: רבי אבא בר פפא gives a different reason for the punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the previous reason is in dispute. רבי אבא בר פפא says יהושע was punished only for keeping ישראל from פריה ורביה for one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי אבא בר פפא. For רבי אבא בר פפא said: יהושע was punished only because he stopped ישראל from פריה ורביה for one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a second opinion. Everyone agrees יהושע went childless, but this view gives a different reason why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views accept the fact that יהושע had no children. They argue only about the cause: ruling הלכה in front of משה, or stopping ישראל from פריה ורביה. The word 'לא... אלא' (only) means that, for רבי אבא בר פפא, the first reason was not why he was punished. The punishment also fits the sin measure for measure: he stopped others from having children, so he had none.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees: this view argues with the previous one
Not... except: only for this reason
The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז"ל treat even one night of lost פריה ורביה for the whole nation. The idea of מידה כנגד מידה (measure for measure) explains why childlessness fits this sin.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Pappa,
for Rabbi Abba bar Pappa said:
Joshua was not punished
except because he prevented the Jewish people
for one night from being fruitful and multiplying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing reason for the same punishment proven in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע's childlessness was a punishment for keeping ישראל from פריה ורביה for one night.

steps.title: The verses about the angel at יריחו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר פפא's source: near יריחו, יהושע met a man with a drawn sword who said, 'I am the captain of the host of ה׳; now I have come.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And it was, when Joshua was by Jericho, he lifted his eyes and saw...' And it is written: 'And he said: I am the captain of the host of the Lord; now I have come...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the verses that רבי אבא בר פפא uses as his source. The next steps will explain what they mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses describe an angel coming to יהושע. The key words are 'עתה באתי': now I have come. The דרש reads this as a rebuke: the angel came because of something wrong happening 'now', which the next lines will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said: introduces a proof verse
Jericho, the first city ישראל fought in ארץ ישראל
Captain of the host of ה׳: an angel
Now I have come: the key words for the דרש

steps.confusionAlert: The verses do not mention פריה ורביה at all. The link to that מצוה comes in step 8, with the tradition that marital relations are forbidden while the ארון is out of its place.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And it came to pass when Joshua was by Jericho'
'that he lifted up his eyes and looked, etc.'
phrases.notes: יהושע ה:יג. He sees a man with a drawn sword.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And he said (to him)'
'I am the captain of the host of the Lord'
'I have now come, etc.'
phrases.notes: יהושע ה:יד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the scriptural source for רבי אבא בר פפא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא בר פפא's view that יהושע was rebuked and punished for a wrong done that night
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע ה:יג-יד, the angel at יריחו

steps.title: The angel lists two failures
steps.stepSummary: The angel tells יהושע: last night you neglected the afternoon תמיד, and now you are neglecting תלמוד תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Last night you neglected the afternoon daily offering, and now you are neglecting Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the angel actually said to יהושע. It is a rebuke for two separate failures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because they were busy preparing for war, the people missed the afternoon תמיד the day before. Tonight they are again occupied with the war and not learning. This sets up יהושע's question about which failure caused the visit.

phrases.english: He said to him: Last night
you neglected the daily afternoon offering,
and now you are neglecting Torah study.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A מדרש filling in the angel's words from the verses in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel rebuked יהושע for neglecting both the תמיד and תלמוד תורה.

steps.title: יהושע asks which failure brought the angel
steps.stepSummary: יהושע asks the angel which of the two failures he came to rebuke.
steps.simpleTranslation: For which of them have you come?
steps.whatsHappening: יהושע asks a clarifying question. It sets up the angel's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two failures were named, but the angel came only now and not last night. יהושע wants to know which failure is the main reason for the visit.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of which of them

phrases.english: For which of them have you come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which of the two failures listed in step 4 is the main one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which failure, the תמיד or תלמוד תורה, caused the angel's visit

steps.title: 'Now I have come': neglecting Torah study is more serious
steps.stepSummary: The angel answers 'עתה באתי': I came now, because of tonight's failure to learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I have now come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The angel answers with the words of the verse. He came because of what is happening now: the people are not learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel did not come last night, when the תמיד was missed. He came only now, when תלמוד תורה was being neglected. This shows that neglecting תורה study is treated as more serious than missing a קרבן.
steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'עתה באתי' teaches that the angel came because of neglected תלמוד תורה, not the missed תמיד. So learning תורה outweighs even the daily קרבן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'last night' with 'now'. The angel was silent about the תמיד last night and came only now, and that timing is the whole proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the idea that תלמוד תורה is greater than the קרבנות.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'I have now come.'
phrases.notes: Meaning: I came now, for tonight's failure to learn תורה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The angel came because of the neglect of תלמוד תורה happening now.

steps.title: Joshua immediately spends the night learning Torah in depth
steps.stepSummary: After the angel's rebuke, יהושע immediately went 'in the midst of the valley' that night. רבי יוחנן explains that this means he went deep into הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away it says: 'And Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.' רבי יוחנן said: this teaches that he went into the depth of הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: יהושע responds to the angel right away by learning תורה all night. רבי יוחנן reads the word 'valley' as a hint to 'depth' of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel said he came because of the failure to learn תורה. So יהושע fixes exactly that failure. The derashah connects עֵמֶק (valley) to עוֹמֶק (depth), so the פסוק shows him learning, not just walking.

keyTerms.meaning: The depth of הלכה, meaning deep Torah study
It teaches, meaning the פסוק is hinting at something

phrases.english: Immediately: 'And Joshua went
phrases.notes: יהושע 8:13

phrases.english: that night into the midst of the valley,'
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
This teaches that he went into the depth of halacha.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: עֵמֶק (valley) and עוֹמֶק (depth)

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד: וַיֵּלֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא בְּתוֹךְ הָעֵמֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how יהושע responded to the angel's answer in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע immediately fixed his neglect by spending the night in deep study of הלכה.

steps.title: Why the delay caused a loss of marital relations
steps.stepSummary: There is a tradition that whenever the ארון and the שכינה are not in their proper place, marital relations are forbidden. This explains how יהושע kept ישראל from פריה ורביה that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we have a tradition: any time that the ארון and the שכינה are not resting in their proper place, people are forbidden in marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a missing piece that connects the story back to רבי אבא בר פפא's claim. It explains why that night meant ישראל lost פריה ורביה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the war, the ארון was not returned to its place that night. Under this tradition, all of ישראל was then forbidden in marital relations. So יהושע's delay is what kept them from פריה ורביה, which proves רבי אבא בר פפא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: And we have a tradition, something learned by tradition

steps.confusionAlert: The angel's rebuke was about תלמוד תורה, but רבי אבא בר פפא said the punishment was for stopping פריה ורביה. This tradition connects the two: the same night of delay also kept the ארון out of place, which forbade marital relations.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא בר פפא's claim is now complete. The night יהושע did not return the ארון to its place was a night when ישראל could not do פריה ורביה, and for this he was punished.

phrases.english: And we have a tradition that any time
that the Ark and the Divine Presence are resting not in their place,
they are forbidden in marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְמִירִי דְּכׇל זְמַן שֶׁאָרוֹן וּשְׁכִינָה שְׁרוּיִין שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof for רבי אבא בר פפא's claim from Step 2 by explaining the link to פריה ורביה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Leaving the ארון out of place forbade marital relations, so יהושע's delay kept ישראל from פריה ורביה for one night.

steps.title: Torah study is greater than the daily offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר איניא in the name of רב learns from this story that תלמוד תורה is greater than offering the תמידין, because the angel said 'עתה באתי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר איניא said in the name of רב: Torah study is greater than offering the daily sacrifices, because the angel told him, 'Now I have come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that takes a lesson from the angel's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both failures happened: the missed afternoon תמיד and the missed learning. The angel only came 'now,' because of the learning. That shows neglecting תלמוד תורה is more serious, so learning is greater than the תמידין.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah study is great, meaning greater in importance

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source that תלמוד תורה is valued even above the daily offerings in the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Inya said in the name of Rav:
Torah study is greater
than offering the daily sacrifices,
since he said to him: 'Now I have come.'
phrases.notes: Refers back to Step 6

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a new general lesson from the angel's answer in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמוד תורה is greater than offering the תמידין.

steps.title: The sin of sleeping in a couple's room
steps.stepSummary: רב ברונא in the name of רב says that anyone who sleeps in a room where a husband and wife stay is described by the פסוק 'You drive out the women of My people from their pleasant homes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ברונא said that רב said: Whoever sleeps in a room where a man and his wife stay, about him the פסוק says: 'The women of My people you drive out from their pleasant homes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about blocking marital relations. It fits with the theme of preventing פריה ורביה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as יהושע was punished for keeping ישראל from marital relations, a person who sleeps in a couple's room also blocks their closeness. רב applies a harsh פסוק from מיכה to him, showing how serious this is.

phrases.english: Rav Beruna said that Rav said:
Whoever sleeps in a room
in which a man and his wife are staying,
about him the verse says:
'The women of My people you drive out
phrases.notes: מיכה 2:9

phrases.english: from their pleasant homes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of preventing marital relations from Step 8 with a new teaching about ordinary people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping in a room where a husband and wife stay, and so blocking their closeness, is condemned by the פסוק in מיכה.

steps.title: The problem applies even when the wife is a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds that sleeping in a couple's room is wrong even when the wife is a נדה and forbidden to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: This applies even if his wife is a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף widens the previous statement of רב ברונא about a guest sleeping in a couple's room. He says it is wrong even when husband and wife are not allowed to be intimate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think there is no harm if the wife is a נדה, since the couple cannot be together anyway. רב יוסף says it still bothers them. A couple wants privacy to be alone together, even when relations are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman during her period of ritual impurity, when relations with her husband are forbidden

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
Even when his wife is a menstruant.
phrases.notes: Even then, the guest disturbs the couple's privacy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲפִילּוּ בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב ברונא's statement in Step 10 to the case of a wife who is a נדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping in a couple's room is wrong even when the wife is a נדה.

steps.title: רבא says the guest deserves a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רב יוסף: if the wife is a נדה, the guest is a blessing, because his presence guards the couple from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If his wife is a נדה, a blessing should come upon him (the guest).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view. In the case of a נדה, the guest is doing something good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reasoning is that a third person in the room keeps the couple from slipping into a sin. So he sees the guest as a protector, not as an intruder.

keyTerms.meaning: May a blessing come upon him

phrases.english: Rava said:
If his wife is a menstruant —
may a blessing come upon him.
phrases.notes: Meaning the guest, who protects the couple from sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִם אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה הִיא תָּבֹא עָלָיו בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רב יוסף's extension in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wife is a נדה, the guest is praiseworthy, because he guards against sin.

steps.title: Rejecting רבא: who guarded them until now?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reasoning. The couple managed perfectly well without a guard until now, so the guest is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Who guarded him until now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבא. It says his argument does not hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This husband has kept the laws of נדה on every other night with no guest in the room. So there is no real need for a guard. The guest only takes away the couple's privacy, and רב יוסף's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: a formula the גמרא uses to reject a statement

steps.whatToRemember: The final view is that one should not sleep in a married couple's room, even when the wife is a נדה. The couple does not need a 'guard,' and the guest only takes away their privacy.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
for until now, who guarded him?
phrases.notes: He kept the laws on his own until now, so he needs no guard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, דְּעַד הָאִידָּנָא מַאן נַטְרֵיהּ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's claim that the guest deserves a blessing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The couple never needed a guard before, so the guest adds no protection and only causes discomfort.

steps.title: A gentile refuses to rent out his rights in the alley
steps.stepSummary: A story: a gentile named לחמן בר ריסתק lived in an alley and would not rent his rights to the Jewish residents, so they brought the problem to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an alley where לחמן בר ריסתק lived. The residents said to him: 'Rent us your rights.' He would not rent to them. They came and told אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the laws of עירובין and tells a real-life case. This step sets up the problem that אביי will solve in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gentile living in a shared alley normally forbids the Jews from carrying there. The usual fix is to rent his rights from him. Here he refuses, so the residents seem stuck and go to אביי for help.

keyTerms.meaning: An alley shared by several courtyards
Rent us your domain (your rights to use the alley)
The name of the gentile who lived in the alley

steps.confusionAlert: Renting the gentile's rights does not mean buying his house. It only means renting his right to use the alley, so that he no longer forbids the Jews from carrying.

phrases.english: There was a certain alley that
Laḥman bar Ristak lived in.
phrases.notes: He was a gentile.

phrases.english: They said to him: Rent us your domain,
he would not rent it to them.
They came and told Abaye.
phrases.notes: This sets up אביי's solution.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מְבוֹאָה דַּהֲוָה דָּיַיר בָּהּ לַחְמָן בַּר רִיסְתַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic section and returns to the main topic of renting a gentile's rights for an עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A case is presented: the gentile refuses to rent, so carrying in the alley seems impossible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the residents can carry in the alley when the gentile refuses to rent out his rights

steps.title: אביי's solution: give your rights to one person
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells the residents to give up their rights in favor of one person. Then only one Jew lives alongside the gentile, and the gentile does not forbid carrying for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Go, give up your rights in favor of one person. Then it is a case of one Jew living with a gentile, and one Jew living with a gentile is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the residents' problem. He uses a known rule to let at least one person carry in the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gentile only forbids carrying when there are two or more Jews in the place. Once everyone gives up their rights to one person, the alley counts as one Jew living with a gentile. That one person may carry, even though the gentile never rented out his rights.

keyTerms.meaning: Renounce your rights (ביטול רשות): giving up your use of the shared area
One Jew living in the same place as a gentile

steps.whatToRemember: A gentile only forbids carrying when at least two Jews share the area with him. With one Jew alone, there is no prohibition. אביי uses this rule through ביטול רשות when the gentile refuses to rent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a practical way around a gentile who refuses to rent. It relies on a rule the גמרא established earlier, so the residents are not left completely stuck.

phrases.english: He said to them: Go
renounce your domains in favor of one person,
so it becomes a case of an individual in the place of a gentile,
and with an individual in the place of a gentile, he does not forbid.
phrases.notes: An established rule: the gentile forbids only when there are two or more Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ בַּטִּילוּ רְשׁוּתַיְיכוּ לְגַבֵּי חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem raised in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone gives up their rights to one person. A single Jew living with a gentile is not forbidden, so he may carry.

steps.title: The residents object: many Jews really do live here
steps.stepSummary: The residents challenge אביי's advice. The lenient rule for one Jew with a gentile exists only because that setup is rare, but here many Jews live in the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Isn't the only reason for the leniency that it is uncommon for people to live like that? But here, they are living here!
steps.whatsHappening: The residents push back on אביי's advice from Step 15. They say his solution does not fit their situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency for one Jew living with a gentile is based on the fact that this rarely happens, so רבנן did not make a decree for it. In this alley many Jews actually live alongside the gentile, which is the common situation where רבנן did decree. Giving up rights on paper does not change who really lives there.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't the reason only... (a challenge formula)

steps.confusionAlert: The residents accept the rule that one Jew with a gentile is lenient. What they question is whether their case counts as 'one Jew,' since many Jews are physically living there.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: The alley residents speak to אביי.

phrases.english: Isn't the reason only
phrases.notes: Opens a challenge by pointing to the reason behind a rule.

phrases.english: that it is not common for people to live that way?
phrases.notes: It is rare for one Jew to live alone with a gentile.

phrases.english: But here, they are in fact living here!
phrases.notes: Many Jews live in this alley, so the situation is not rare.

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's advice to give up rights in favor of one person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The leniency depends on the situation being rare. Here many Jews really live with the gentile, so the reason for the leniency does not apply.

steps.title: אביי answers: giving up rights to one person is itself rare
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies that a case where everyone gives up rights to one person is uncommon, and רבנן do not make decrees for uncommon cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Any case of giving up their rights in favor of one person is an uncommon thing. And for an uncommon thing, רבנן did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his advice. He moves the focus from how many Jews live there to how unusual the whole arrangement is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי agrees that the leniency depends on rarity. He says that rarity is still present here, because it is unusual for a whole alley to give up its rights to one person. Since רבנן only decreed against common situations, this unusual setup stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving up (nullifying) their rights or domains
The Sages did not make a decree about it

steps.whatToRemember: מילתא דלא שכיחא לא גזרו בה רבנן: the Sages did not make protective decrees for rare situations. אביי shows that his arrangement is itself rare.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that the Sages do not decree for rare situations, appears throughout ש״ס and is a common tool for explaining when a rabbinic decree applies.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: אביי answers the residents.

phrases.english: Any case of giving up their domains in favor of one person
is an uncommon thing,
and for an uncommon thing,
the Sages did not make a decree.
phrases.notes: So the leniency still applies.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what makes the case rare
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case counts as common because many Jews physically live in the alley.
steps.terutzMaskana: The arrangement of giving up rights to one person is itself rare, so no decree applies.

steps.title: רב הונא brings אביי's ruling to רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע reports אביי's ruling to רבא, and רבא begins to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, went and said this teaching before רבא. He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to show רבא's reaction to אביי's ruling, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is now brought before a second great authority, רבא. This tells us that רבא's opinion on אביי's solution is coming next, and it may agree or disagree.
